records.name: Vika
records.facts_used: Vika: The name belongs to the Victoria / Viktorija family. Its linguistic basis is explained through Latin victoria, victory. The historical connection survives changes of spelling and endings across languages. The beginning of a particular local form’s use must be distinguished from the earlier history of the whole family. Siliņš’s dictionary dates the use of Vika: 1969, Bauska. Its calendar year is 1889. This records use of the particular name in Latvia. The entry cannot automatically be transferred to similar spellings or treated as the moment the entire name family originated.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.

records.name: Vilbutas
records.facts_used: Vilbutas: The Lithuanian compound name combines vil- (viltis), hope, and but- (būti), to be. These vocabulary comparisons explain its individual stems. They should not be turned into a single modern sentence or a description of personality: a personal name’s history is distinct from its bearer’s qualities. The 1964 calendar reprinted in Salys’s 1983 volume gives Vilbutas (Vilas) on 23 December. This is a concrete printed example of the form’s use. Its position in the historical calendar need not match every modern calendar and is not the name’s invention date.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.

records.name: Eugenia
records.facts_used: Eugenia: The name belongs to the Eugenia / Eugenija / Eugenius family. Its linguistic basis is explained through Greek eugenēs, well born, from eu and genēs. The historical connection survives changes of spelling and endings across languages. The beginning of a particular local form’s use must be distinguished from the earlier history of the whole family. The first page of Leole’s December 2005 issue uses the exact spelling Eugenia. The local name column shows that this form was discussed in Estonian print. This dated evidence is neither a first birth record nor the year the name was invented.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
